name: Tools: build and ship
description: Code hosting, CI, issue trackers, cloud, monitoring, identity.

cards.subject: A commit
says: records a snapshot of the staged changes with a message
is identified by a hash
is normally undone by adding a new commit rather than by deleting it
cards.use: want a named, reviewable point in history
not: stores only the lines that changed and no snapshot of the project at all

cards.subject: A branch
says: is a movable pointer to a commit
lets work proceed in isolation from the main line
is cheap to create in Git because it copies no files
cards.use: want to try a change without disturbing the main line
not: is a full copy of every file in the repository

cards.subject: A merge
says: combines the histories of two branches
can create a merge commit with two parents
stops and asks for help when both sides edited the same lines
cards.use: want to bring a finished branch into the main line and keep its history intact
not: always rewrites the commits of the branch being merged

cards.subject: A rebase
says: replays commits on top of a different base commit
gives the replayed commits new hashes
produces a linear history without merge commits
cards.use: want your branch to sit on the latest main before review
not: is safe to run on a branch other people have already pulled

cards.subject: A cherry-pick
says: applies one chosen commit onto the current branch
creates a new commit with a different hash from the original
suits carrying a single fix onto a release branch
cards.use: need one fix from another branch and not the rest of its work
not: merges the whole of another branch into the current one

cards.subject: A squash merge
says: collapses all of a branch's commits into one commit on the target
keeps the target's history short and one-commit-per-change
discards the individual commits from the target branch's history
cards.use: want one tidy commit per pull request on main
not: keeps every original commit as it was on the target branch

cards.subject: A merge conflict
says: happens when two changes touch the same lines
is shown in the file with conflict markers
must be resolved by a person choosing the final content
cards.use: see conflict markers after pulling
not: means the repository is corrupted and must be recloned

cards.subject: git stash
says: shelves uncommitted changes and leaves a clean working tree
lets you switch branch without committing half-done work
stores the shelved work so it can be applied again later
cards.use: need to switch branch but are not ready to commit
not: pushes your uncommitted changes to the remote

cards.subject: git revert
says: creates a new commit that undoes an earlier commit
leaves the earlier commit in history
is the safe way to back out a change that is already shared
cards.use: must undo a commit that others have already pulled
not: deletes the earlier commit from the history

cards.subject: git reset --hard
says: moves the branch pointer and overwrites the working tree
discards uncommitted changes with no undo from Git
rewrites history when used on commits that were already shared
cards.use: deliberately want to throw away local work and match a commit exactly
not: keeps your uncommitted changes safe in the stash

cards.subject: git reflog
says: records where HEAD has pointed over recent history
lets you find a commit that no branch points to any more
can recover work after a bad reset or rebase
cards.use: lost commits after a rebase and need to find them
not: is a log kept on the remote server for every user

cards.subject: git bisect
says: binary-searches the history for the commit that introduced a bug
needs a known good commit and a known bad commit to start
finds the culprit in a number of steps that grows with the logarithm of the commits
cards.use: know a bug is new but not which of many commits caused it
not: lists every file changed in the last commit

cards.subject: A pull request
says: proposes merging one branch into another
hosts review comments and discussion beside the diff
is where automated checks report their status
cards.use: want a teammate to review a change before it joins main
not: pushes the change straight to main without review

cards.subject: A draft pull request
says: signals that the change is not ready for review
can be marked ready when the author is done
lets CI run while review has not yet been requested
cards.use: want early feedback and CI results on unfinished work
not: cannot be updated with new commits

cards.subject: Branch protection
says: blocks direct pushes to a chosen branch
can require reviews and passing checks before merging
can stop force pushes and branch deletion
cards.use: want to guarantee nothing reaches main without passing checks
not: only affects people with read access

cards.subject: A required status check
says: must pass before a pull request can be merged
is reported to the pull request by CI
blocks the merge button while it is failing or missing
cards.use: want the merge button disabled until tests pass
not: is optional information that never blocks a merge

cards.subject: A CODEOWNERS file
says: maps file paths to the people or teams who own them
requests review automatically from the owners of changed files
can be enforced so owners must approve changes to their paths
cards.use: want changes to the payments folder always reviewed by the payments team
not: controls who may read the repository

cards.subject: A fork
says: is a server-side copy of a repository under another account
lets outside contributors propose changes through pull requests
does not give the contributor write access to the original
cards.use: are contributing to a project where you have no write access
not: is the same thing as a branch of the original repository

cards.subject: A webhook
says: sends an HTTP request to a URL when an event happens
lets another system react to pushes or pull request events
pushes events out, where polling would repeatedly ask for them
cards.use: want an external system told the moment code is pushed
not: pulls code from the server on a timer

cards.subject: A deploy key
says: is an SSH key that grants access to a single repository
is usually read-only unless write is explicitly enabled
suits a server that only needs to pull one project's code
cards.use: have a server that must clone just one private repository
not: gives the holder access to every repository the owner can see

cards.subject: A personal access token
says: acts with the permissions of the user who created it
should be scoped narrowly and given an expiry
can be revoked without changing the account password
cards.use: need a script to call the hosting API as yourself
not: is safe to commit to the repository if it is short-lived

cards.subject: Continuous integration
says: merges changes into the shared branch often
builds and tests every change automatically
surfaces integration problems while they are small
cards.use: want every push checked automatically
not: means releasing to customers on every commit

cards.subject: Continuous delivery
says: keeps every change in a releasable state
automates the path to production but leaves the final release as a human decision
makes releases routine and low-drama
cards.use: want to be able to ship at any time but choose the moment
not: pushes every passing commit to production with no human step

cards.subject: Continuous deployment
says: releases every change that passes the pipeline to production automatically
removes the manual approval step
depends heavily on trustworthy automated tests and monitoring
cards.use: want no human gate between a green build and production
not: waits for a manual release sign-off after each green build

cards.subject: A pipeline
says: is a sequence of automated stages such as build, test and deploy
stops at the first stage that fails by default
is defined in a configuration file kept with the code
cards.use: want build, test and deploy to run in a fixed order
not: is a manual checklist a person follows

cards.subject: A workflow trigger
says: decides which events start a pipeline run
can be a push, a pull request, a schedule or a manual dispatch
controls whether a run happens at all
cards.use: want a pipeline to run only on pushes to main and by hand
not: is the secret that authorises the deploy

cards.subject: A CI runner
says: is the machine that executes the pipeline's jobs
can be hosted by the CI vendor or run on your own server
starts each job with a fresh environment on hosted runners
cards.use: are choosing where pipeline jobs actually run
not: is the test framework that decides pass or fail

cards.subject: A build artifact
says: is a file or package produced by a build
can be passed from one job to a later job
lets the thing that was tested be the thing that is deployed
cards.use: want the deploy stage to use exactly what the test stage verified
not: is the log of a failed test run

cards.subject: A matrix build
says: runs the same job across combinations of settings
can test several language versions or operating systems at once
multiplies the number of job runs with each added dimension
cards.use: must prove the code works on three Node versions
not: runs the jobs one after another on a single machine

cards.subject: A build cache
says: stores dependencies or build output between runs
speeds up pipelines by skipping repeated work
can serve stale results if its key does not change when inputs do
cards.use: want npm installs to stop dominating pipeline time
not: guarantees a clean build every run

cards.subject: A concurrency group
says: limits how many runs of a workflow execute together
can queue new runs instead of cancelling one in progress
prevents two deploys from overlapping
cards.use: must stop two deploy runs from racing each other
not: splits a job across several runners

cards.subject: A linter
says: flags style problems and suspicious code patterns
analyses source without running it
can often fix simple issues automatically
cards.use: want consistent style and early warnings before tests
not: checks the running service for uptime

cards.subject: A type checker
says: verifies that values are used consistently with their declared types
catches mismatches before the code runs
runs on source without executing it
cards.use: want mistakes like passing a string where a number is expected caught early
not: measures how much code the tests execute

cards.subject: A unit test
says: exercises one small piece of code in isolation
runs quickly and without outside services
points to a precise failing function when it breaks
cards.use: want fast feedback on one function's logic
not: drives the whole product through a real browser

cards.subject: An integration test
says: checks that several components work together
often runs against a real database or service
is slower and needs more setup than a unit test
cards.use: need to prove the app and its real database agree
not: mocks out every dependency so none is used

cards.subject: An end-to-end test
says: drives the whole system the way a user would
covers the full path from interface to storage
is the slowest and most fragile layer of the test pyramid
cards.use: want to confirm the sign-up journey works from the browser down
not: tests one function with no dependencies

cards.subject: A smoke test
says: runs a few basic checks that the deployed system is alive
fails fast when something fundamental is broken
is a shallow check run right after a deploy
cards.use: want a quick yes or no that the release is not obviously broken
not: proves every feature works exhaustively

cards.subject: A container image scan
says: inspects an image's packages for known vulnerabilities
can fail a pipeline when serious findings appear
only knows about vulnerabilities that are already published
cards.use: want known-vulnerable packages caught before an image ships
not: proves the image contains no vulnerabilities at all

cards.subject: A flaky test
says: passes and fails on the same code without any change
erodes trust in the pipeline when left alone
is often caused by timing, shared state or outside services
cards.use: see a test fail once and pass on rerun with no code change
not: is a sign the test is perfectly reliable

cards.subject: A health check probe
says: asks the running service whether it is up
expects a success status such as HTTP 200
lets a deploy fail when the app does not come back
cards.use: want a deploy to prove the app actually answers
not: measures how much of the code is tested

cards.subject: A rolling deployment
says: replaces instances with the new version a few at a time
keeps some capacity serving traffic throughout
runs the old and new versions side by side for a while
cards.use: have several instances and want no full outage
not: switches all traffic at once to a complete second environment

cards.subject: A blue-green deployment
says: keeps two full production environments, one live and one idle
switches traffic from one to the other when ready
makes rollback a matter of switching back
cards.use: want an instant switch-over and an instant way back
not: sends the new version to a small percentage of users first

cards.subject: A canary release
says: sends the new version to a small share of traffic first
watches metrics before widening the rollout
limits the number of users hurt by a bad release
cards.use: want real traffic to test the release before everyone gets it
not: replaces every instance simultaneously

cards.subject: A feature flag
says: turns a feature on or off without a new deploy
separates deploying code from releasing a feature
lets unfinished code ship hidden
cards.use: want to merge unfinished work to main without users seeing it
not: is a pull request label that marks urgent work

cards.subject: A rollback
says: returns production to a previous known-good version
is the fastest response to a release that breaks things
needs the old version or build to still be available
cards.use: released a version that is failing and need the last good one back
not: adds a new commit that fixes the bug going forward

cards.subject: Rolling forward
says: fixes a bad release by shipping a new corrected version
is often the only choice after a data migration that cannot be undone
needs a fast, trusted pipeline to be safe
cards.use: cannot go back because the database schema already changed
not: restores the previous version from backup

cards.subject: A staging environment
says: mirrors production closely for final checks
lets a release be tried without affecting real users
is only as useful as it is similar to production
cards.use: want to try a release somewhere that looks like production
not: is the live environment customers use

cards.subject: A database migration
says: changes the database schema in a controlled, repeatable way
is kept as code and applied in order
runs as part of the deploy
cards.use: need a new column in the production database
not: is a copy of the database taken for backup

cards.subject: Expand and contract
says: adds a new schema element alongside the old before removing the old
lets old and new code versions run against the same database
splits a breaking change into several safe releases
cards.use: must rename a column with no downtime
not: drops the old column in the same release that adds the new one

cards.subject: Infrastructure as code
says: describes servers and services in version-controlled files
makes environments reproducible and reviewable
reduces drift between what is documented and what exists
cards.use: want server setup recorded, reviewed and repeatable
not: means configuring each server by hand and documenting it afterwards

cards.subject: An issue
says: represents one unit of work or one problem
has an owner and a state
gives code changes something to link back to
cards.use: want a piece of work to be visible and owned
not: is a commit message

cards.subject: A backlog
says: holds work that is not yet scheduled
is ordered so the most valuable work sits at the top
needs regular grooming or it becomes a graveyard
cards.use: want one ordered list of work waiting to be done
not: lists only the items in the current sprint

cards.subject: Triage
says: sorts new issues by validity, severity and owner
decides what to do with a report before work starts
separates duplicates and noise from real work
cards.use: face a stream of new reports and must decide which matter
not: fixes the bug the moment it is reported

cards.subject: Acceptance criteria
says: state the conditions that must hold for the work to be accepted
are written before the work begins
make done a testable claim
cards.use: want a shared, checkable meaning of finished for one issue
not: list the people who must approve the release

cards.subject: The definition of done
says: applies to every item the team finishes
sets common standards such as tested, reviewed and documented
does not change from one issue to the next
cards.use: want one quality bar shared across all work
not: describes the specific outcome of a single issue

cards.subject: A work-in-progress limit
says: caps how many items can be in a state at once
pushes the team to finish work before starting more
exposes bottlenecks when a column fills up
cards.use: see many half-finished items and nothing shipping
not: raises the number of tasks each person starts

cards.subject: Severity
says: measures how much damage a defect does
describes impact, such as data loss versus a cosmetic flaw
is separate from the order in which work is scheduled
cards.use: must describe how bad a defect is
not: says when the team will schedule the fix

cards.subject: Priority
says: says how soon something should be dealt with
reflects business context as well as damage
can differ from severity, for example a cosmetic flaw on the home page
cards.use: must decide what the team works on first
not: measures how much technical damage a defect causes

cards.subject: Infrastructure as a service
says: rents virtual machines, storage and networks
leaves the operating system and everything above it to the customer
gives the most control among the cloud service models
cards.use: want a raw virtual machine you manage yourself
not: hides the operating system and runs your code for you

cards.subject: Platform as a service
says: runs your application without you managing the servers
handles the operating system and runtime for you
takes the code or a container and gives back a running app
cards.use: want to push code and let the provider run it
not: gives you only a bare virtual machine

cards.subject: A serverless function
says: runs code in response to an event
scales with demand and can scale to zero
bills for execution rather than for idle servers
cards.use: have small event-driven code that is idle most of the time
not: keeps a long-lived server always running for you to manage

cards.subject: Object storage
says: stores files as objects addressed by a key in a bucket
scales to very large amounts of data
is suited to images, backups and static assets rather than databases
cards.use: need cheap, durable storage for uploads and backups
not: is a low-latency block device attached to one machine

cards.subject: Block storage
says: provides a disk volume attached to a virtual machine
behaves like a local drive with a filesystem
is what databases on a virtual machine typically sit on
cards.use: need a disk for a database running on a virtual machine
not: stores objects behind web URLs addressed by key

cards.subject: A managed database
says: is run by the provider, who handles patching and backups
reduces the operational work of running a database
still needs the customer to design schema and access
cards.use: want a database without maintaining the server
not: needs you to install and patch the database engine

cards.subject: A container registry
says: stores and serves container images
is where a deploy pulls an image by name and tag
lets the same image move from CI to production
cards.use: need somewhere to publish images that servers can pull
not: runs containers on a cluster

cards.subject: A container orchestrator
says: schedules containers across a cluster of machines
restarts failed containers and scales their number
handles service discovery and rolling updates
cards.use: run many containers and need them kept alive and spread out
not: only stores container images

cards.subject: A content delivery network
says: caches content at locations close to visitors
reduces load on the origin server
can also provide protection and TLS in front of the origin
cards.use: want static assets served fast worldwide and less traffic on the origin
not: stores your primary database

cards.subject: A load balancer
says: spreads incoming requests across several instances
uses health checks to avoid unhealthy instances
removes a single instance as a single point of failure
cards.use: have several app instances and one public address
not: stores the application's secrets

cards.subject: A managed secrets store
says: keeps credentials encrypted and access-controlled
lets applications fetch secrets at runtime
records who read each secret
cards.use: want secrets out of code and config files
not: is a text file in the repository listing keys

cards.subject: A virtual private server
says: is a rented virtual machine with root access
runs one operating system that the customer maintains
is how a small app is often hosted behind a reverse proxy
cards.use: host a small app on one machine you fully control
not: scales automatically to zero when idle

cards.subject: An uptime check
says: asks from outside whether a service responds
raises an alert when requests fail
answers whether the service is up and not whether it is healthy inside
cards.use: want to know the moment the site stops answering
not: explains why a request was slow

cards.subject: A metric
says: is a numeric measurement sampled over time
suits trends, dashboards and alert thresholds
is cheap to store compared with raw events
cards.use: want to chart request rate or memory use over weeks
not: is a record of one individual event with its details

cards.subject: A log line
says: records one event with its context
is what you search when you need the detail of a failure
grows in volume as traffic grows
cards.use: need to see exactly what happened in one failed request
not: is a number sampled at regular intervals

cards.subject: A trace
says: follows one request across several services
breaks the request into timed spans
shows which hop made a request slow
cards.use: need to find which service in a chain adds the latency
not: counts total requests per minute

cards.subject: Log aggregation
says: collects logs from many machines into one searchable place
lets you search across services at once
depends on shippers that forward logs from each host
cards.use: have logs scattered across servers and need to search them together
not: deletes old logs to save space

cards.subject: An alert threshold
says: sets the value at which a metric raises an alert
decides when a person is paged
is too tight when it produces many alerts that need no action
cards.use: want to be told when error rate crosses a limit
not: is the time period logs are kept for

cards.subject: Alert fatigue
says: happens when too many alerts train people to ignore them
hides the one alert that matters among noise
is cured by alerting on symptoms and removing alerts nobody acts on
cards.use: find the team has stopped reading the alert channel
not: is caused by having too few alerts

cards.subject: A service level objective
says: sets a target for reliability such as a share of successful requests
is measured over a defined time window
gives a number to argue about instead of a feeling
cards.use: need an agreed target for how reliable a service must be
not: is the contract that pays customers back when missed

cards.subject: An error budget
says: is the amount of unreliability an objective allows
shrinks as failures use it up
can justify slowing releases when it is spent
cards.use: must decide whether to ship risky changes or focus on stability
not: is the money set aside for fixing outages

cards.subject: A runbook
says: gives step-by-step instructions for handling a known alert
reduces guesswork during an incident
should be updated after each incident that taught something new
cards.use: want the person paged at night to know what to check first
not: is the record of why an incident happened

cards.subject: A blameless postmortem
says: examines what happened and why after an incident
focuses on the system and process rather than individuals
ends with agreed follow-up actions
cards.use: want learning from an outage and not a hunt for someone to blame
not: names the engineer responsible so they can be disciplined

cards.subject: Observability
says: lets you ask new questions about a system from the data it emits
combines metrics, logs and traces
goes beyond checking known failure modes with set dashboards
cards.use: need to debug failures nobody predicted
not: is just having a dashboard of CPU use

cards.subject: Single sign-on
says: lets one login give access to many applications
centralises authentication in one identity provider
means removing a person once cuts their access everywhere
cards.use: want staff to log in once for all work tools
not: gives every application its own separate password

cards.subject: An identity provider
says: holds user identities and authenticates them
issues proof of login to other applications
is the central system behind single sign-on
cards.use: need one trusted place that says who a person is
not: is the application the user is trying to use

cards.subject: SAML
says: exchanges signed XML assertions between identity provider and application
is common in older enterprise single sign-on
is browser-based and redirects the user to log in
cards.use: integrate with an enterprise identity provider that expects XML assertions
not: is a JSON-based protocol designed for mobile apps

cards.subject: OpenID Connect
says: adds an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0
returns an ID token describing who logged in
uses JSON and JSON Web Tokens
cards.use: want users to log in with an identity provider and learn who they are
not: replaces OAuth 2.0 as a separate protocol

cards.subject: OAuth 2.0
says: lets an application act on a user's behalf without their password
issues access tokens with limited scopes
is about delegated authorisation rather than proving identity
cards.use: want a third party app to read some of a user's data without handing over the password
not: is mainly an authentication standard that identifies the user

cards.subject: Multi-factor authentication
says: requires more than one kind of proof to log in
combines something you know with something you have or are
limits the damage from a stolen password
cards.use: want a stolen password alone to be useless
not: means typing the password twice

cards.subject: Role-based access control
says: grants permissions through roles rather than to individuals
makes access easier to review and change in bulk
assigns people to roles that match their job
cards.use: want access based on job function
not: gives each person a hand-picked list of permissions

cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives an identity only the access it needs
limits the harm from a mistake or a stolen credential
applies to people, services and tokens alike
cards.use: are deciding how much access a new deploy token should have
not: gives everyone admin access so work is never blocked

cards.subject: SCIM provisioning
says: automates creating, updating and removing user accounts across applications
reads from the identity provider as the source of truth
closes the gap where leavers keep accounts in tools
cards.use: want accounts in every tool created and removed automatically
not: authenticates the user at login

cards.subject: A service account
says: is an identity used by software and not a person
should hold only the permissions its job needs
should have its credentials rotated and stored as secrets
cards.use: need a pipeline to act without a person's login
not: is the personal account of the team lead shared with the pipeline

cards.subject: An access review
says: checks periodically who has access to what
removes access that is no longer needed
catches leavers and role changes that were missed
cards.use: want to find stale accounts and excess permissions
not: is a one-time check when an account is created

cards.subject: CI-only dummy secrets
says: let pipelines run without production credentials
are values that work only inside the test run
remove the risk of a leaked CI log exposing something real
cards.use: need a test job to start with credentials it will not misuse
not: are copies of production secrets stored for convenience

cards.subject: Secret scoping
says: limits a secret to the jobs or environments that need it
keeps a production credential away from pull request builds
reduces the blast radius if one job is compromised
cards.use: want only the deploy job to see the production key
not: shares every secret with every job

cards.subject: Secret rotation
says: replaces a credential with a new one on a schedule or after exposure
shortens how long a leaked secret stays useful
is easier when secrets are fetched at runtime
cards.use: suspect a key was exposed and need it dead
not: adds a second copy of the same key

cards.subject: Secret scanning
says: searches code and history for committed credentials
can block a push or alert the owner
does not remove a credential that has already leaked
cards.use: want to catch an accidentally committed token
not: encrypts secrets stored in the repository

cards.subject: A leaked secret in history
says: remains in git history after a later commit deletes the file
must be treated as compromised and rotated
is not fixed by removing the line in a new commit
cards.use: found a password in an old commit
not: is safe once the file is deleted in the latest commit

cards.subject: Pinning third-party actions
says: fixes a pipeline step to a specific immutable version or commit
stops a changed upstream action from altering your pipeline unseen
makes builds reproducible
cards.use: want protection from a compromised or changed third-party step
not: always picks up the newest release automatically

cards.subject: A lockfile
says: records the exact resolved versions of every dependency
makes installs repeatable across machines
is committed alongside the manifest
cards.use: want CI to install exactly the versions you tested
not: is a file that stops two deploys running together

cards.subject: A restore test
says: proves a backup can actually be restored
finds a broken backup before the disaster
checks how long recovery really takes
cards.use: have backups and no evidence they work
not: counts how many backups were taken

cards.subject: An approval gate
says: pauses a pipeline until a named person approves
is often placed before a production deploy
adds a human check to an otherwise automated path
cards.use: want a person to confirm before production changes
not: skips the pipeline's tests

cards.subject: The deploy.sh script
says: is the single script that deploys gglearn
is run by the GitHub Actions workflow on every push to main
syncs the code and then runs the server-side steps over ssh
cards.use: want to know what deploys gglearn
not: is a script run by hand only on the developer's laptop

cards.subject: The GitHub Actions deploy workflow
says: runs deploy.sh on every push to main
can also be started by hand with workflow_dispatch
checks that four repository secrets exist before deploying
cards.use: want to know what starts a gglearn deploy
not: runs only on a nightly schedule

cards.subject: The four repository secrets
says: hold an ssh key, a host, a user and known-hosts for the server
are checked by the workflow before it does anything
let the workflow write the ssh config for the alias gglink-live
cards.use: are wondering what credentials the gglearn workflow needs
not: hold the application's database password and app secret

cards.subject: The workflow's concurrency setting
says: queues deploys instead of cancelling one that is half-way
stops a newer push from interrupting a running deploy
protects the server from a deploy being cut off in the middle
cards.use: push twice in quick succession and wonder what the first run does
not: cancels the older run as soon as a newer one starts

cards.subject: The rsync step with --delete
says: copies the code to /var/www/gglearn.gglink.co.uk
removes server files not present in the source unless excluded
excludes node_modules, .next, .git, the SQLite files and .env files
cards.use: want to know why the database survives each deploy
not: copies the SQLite database to the server on every deploy

cards.subject: The flock on the server
says: is taken so two deploys cannot overlap
covers the remote steps run on the server
makes a second deploy wait instead of running together with the first
cards.use: want to know what prevents overlapping deploys on the server itself
not: encrypts the database file while the build runs

cards.subject: npm ci in the deploy
says: installs exactly what the lockfile specifies
runs on the server before the build
fails rather than silently updating the lockfile
cards.use: need to know how the server gets its dependencies
not: updates dependencies to their newest versions

cards.subject: drizzle-kit push in the deploy
says: applies the schema to the SQLite database
deliberately runs without --force
stops the deploy when a change would delete rows
cards.use: are adding a column and want to know how the deploy updates the schema
not: always accepts destructive schema changes

cards.subject: next build in the deploy
says: builds the production version of the app on the server
runs after the dependencies and schema step
is one of the only checks in the gglearn workflow, with the health probe
cards.use: want to know which gglearn deploy step can catch a compile error
not: runs the full unit test suite

cards.subject: pm2 startOrRestart and pm2 save
says: starts the app from the ecosystem file or restarts it if it is already running
is followed by saving the process list
keeps the app supervised on the server
cards.use: want to know how the new gglearn build begins serving
not: reloads Apache with the new virtual host

cards.subject: The gglearn health poll
says: requests http://127.0.0.1:3400/ up to ten times
fails the deploy unless it receives HTTP 200
prints recent pm2 error logs when it fails
cards.use: want to know how gglearn knows a deploy worked
not: only checks that the build command exited

cards.subject: No test or lint step in the gglearn workflow
says: leaves the build and the health probe as the only checks
means a failing test would not stop a deploy
is a gap compared with a pipeline that runs tests first
cards.use: are asked what protects gglearn from a logic bug
not: is covered by the vitest suite that runs in the workflow

cards.subject: The X-Forwarded-For header
says: carries the visitor's address when a proxy sits in front
can be forged if clients reach the origin directly
is trusted only when all traffic really passes through the proxy
cards.use: want to know where the app reads the visitor address from
not: is added by the visitor's browser and can always be trusted

cards.subject: Origin lockdown
says: restricts the origin server to accept traffic only from Cloudflare
stops people bypassing the proxy and its protections
protects rate limiting and logging from spoofed addresses
cards.use: want to stop attackers hitting the server directly
not: hides the origin server's address with no firewall rule

cards.subject: apache-cloudflare-only.conf
says: is a Location block that allows localhost and Cloudflare's published ranges
is pulled into the vhost with an Include
denies every other address
cards.use: want to know where the gglearn allow-list lives
not: is the file that holds Cloudflare's API token

cards.subject: Include instead of IncludeOptional
says: makes Apache refuse to start if the file is missing
avoids quietly serving everyone when the allow-list is lost
fails loudly rather than open
cards.use: are asked why a missing file should stop Apache
not: lets Apache start without the file and continue

cards.subject: update-cloudflare-ips.sh
says: regenerates the allow-list from Cloudflare's published lists
refuses to write if the fetched lists look wrong
avoids producing an empty allow-list that locks everyone out
cards.use: need to refresh the list of Cloudflare addresses
not: edits Apache's config and reloads it in one step

cards.subject: The certbot port 80 vhost copy
says: is made into the port 443 vhost
can drop the allow-list unless the Include line is also present
needs the same Include line in both vhosts
cards.use: added TLS with certbot and need the lockdown preserved
not: links the 443 vhost to the 80 vhost, so edits always carry over

cards.subject: Full (strict) SSL mode
says: encrypts traffic between Cloudflare and the origin and validates the certificate
is required for ggmoney according to its DEPLOY.md
protects tokens on the Cloudflare-to-origin hop
cards.use: need the Cloudflare to origin hop encrypted and verified
not: leaves the Cloudflare to origin hop unencrypted

cards.subject: Flexible SSL mode
says: encrypts only the visitor-to-Cloudflare hop
sends traffic from Cloudflare to the origin unencrypted
would expose OAuth tokens on the origin hop
cards.use: are asked why Flexible is wrong for sites that handle OAuth tokens
not: validates the certificate on the origin

cards.subject: Let's Encrypt and certbot's timer
says: issue and renew the origin certificates
renew automatically on a timer
give the origin a certificate Cloudflare can validate
cards.use: want to know how origin certificates stay valid
not: require manual renewal by an administrator each year

cards.subject: Apache as reverse proxy
says: forwards requests to a local Node process
sits behind Cloudflare on the origin
terminates TLS on the origin for the vhost
cards.use: want to know what receives requests before the Node app
not: serves the app's pages by running the Next code itself

cards.subject: ggsocial's two pm2 processes
says: are ggsocial-web and ggsocial-scheduler
split serving the site from sending scheduled posts
include a scheduler that calls cron endpoints
cards.use: want to know what keeps ggsocial's scheduled posts going out
not: are two copies of the web server for load sharing

cards.subject: ggsocial's Postgres in Docker
says: is the database, running in a Docker container
is backed up by the deploy script before changes
has backups that are not scheduled automatically
cards.use: want to know where ggsocial keeps its data
not: is a SQLite file excluded from rsync

cards.subject: npm run deploy
says: is run from a laptop to deploy ggsocial
warns about uncommitted changes first
runs the server half over ssh after the local checks
cards.use: want to know how a ggsocial deploy starts
not: is triggered by a push to main

cards.subject: ggsocial's local pre-flight checks
says: run tsc, lint and the vitest tests on the laptop
stop the deploy if any of them fails
depend on the deployer running the script
cards.use: want to know where ggsocial's tests run
not: run in a remote CI job on every pull request

cards.subject: The server-side .env
says: holds ggsocial's secrets only on the server
must be excluded from rsync --delete
is checked for existence by the server half
cards.use: want to know where ggsocial's secrets live
not: is committed to the repository so deploys can copy it

cards.subject: Deleting .env through rsync
says: happens if rsync --delete does not exclude it
loses the app secret
logs everyone out and makes stored tokens unreadable
cards.use: are asked what goes wrong without the exclusion
not: is harmless because the file is recreated from the repository

cards.subject: ggsocial's fresh-directory build
says: builds into a new directory and then swaps it in
keeps the old build serving while the new one compiles
shortens the time the site shows a broken state
cards.use: want to know how ggsocial avoids downtime during a build
not: stops the app before building in place

cards.subject: ggsocial's schema push before restart
says: applies the database schema before restarting the app
stops new code starting against an old schema
comes after the database backup
cards.use: want to know the order of schema and restart
not: restarts the processes before pushing the schema

cards.subject: The fish login shell trap
says: cannot parse some bash syntax
is why the script streams commands into bash -s
makes plain ssh commands behave unexpectedly
cards.use: saw a deploy command fail on the server with a syntax error
not: is solved by installing a newer Node version

cards.subject: The wrong-Node trap
says: comes from a login shell picking a different Node version
is avoided by putting the system Node first
can break builds with version mismatches
cards.use: found the server building with an unexpected Node version
not: is fixed by committing node_modules

cards.subject: The Apache vhost copy trap
says: means the live HTTPS vhost is a copy and not a symlink
lets edits to sites-available pass configtest yet change nothing
needs the live file edited too
cards.use: edited sites-available and saw no change on the live site
not: is avoided because the live vhost links to sites-available

cards.subject: Moksy's CI triggers
says: run on pushes and pull requests
cover several jobs in one workflow
start lint, tests, image scan and smoke tests
cards.use: want to know when Moksy's CI runs
not: run only when a release is tagged

cards.subject: Moksy's integration tests
says: run against a real MongoDB service container
exercise the services with a real database
sit alongside the unit tests
cards.use: want to know how Moksy tests against a database
not: mock the database in every test

cards.subject: Moksy's gateway smoke tests
says: check the gateway as a shallow liveness test
are one of the jobs in the CI workflow
belong to the same workflow as lint and the image scan
cards.use: want to know what checks the gateway in CI
not: run the entire integration suite

cards.subject: Moksy's container image scan
says: is a CI job that scans images
looks for known vulnerabilities in the image
runs along the lint and test jobs
cards.use: want to know which job checks image security in Moksy
not: scans the source for style problems

cards.subject: Moksy's shared top-level secrets
says: are declared once at the top of the CI workflow
prevent drift between jobs
replaced a copy-per-job approach that once left a secret too short
cards.use: want to know why Moksy declares CI secrets once
not: are copied into every job for independence

cards.subject: Moksy's CI dummy values
says: are CI-only values and not real secrets
follow the habit of never reusing real secrets in CI
mean a leaked log reveals nothing real
cards.use: want to know what secrets Moksy CI uses
not: are the production credentials copied for tests

cards.subject: Moksy's observability folders
says: include Loki, Promtail and an alert dispatcher
hold logging and alerting setup in the Moksy repo
are not what the small Next apps use, which rely on pm2 and Apache logs
cards.use: want to know what monitoring Moksy's repo contains

qa.q: What is the main purpose of continuous integration?
qa.right: To build and test every change automatically so integration problems show up early
wrong: To deploy every change to customers with no checks
To store the source code on a server
To replace code review with automated approval
qa.why: CI runs automated builds and tests on each change.

qa.q: Which command shows the state of your working tree in Git?
qa.right: git status
qa.why: git status lists staged, unstaged and untracked files.

qa.q: What does a pull request ask for?
qa.right: A review and merge of one branch into another
wrong: A copy of the repository on another account
qa.why: A pull request proposes a merge and hosts review.

qa.q: What does multi-factor authentication add to a password login?
qa.right: A second, different kind of proof
wrong: A second copy of the same password
qa.why: MFA combines different kinds of factor.

qa.q: Why do teams keep work in an issue tracker?
qa.right: So work has an owner, a state and something code changes can link to
wrong: So commits can be deleted later
So no one needs to communicate
qa.why: Trackers make work visible and traceable.

qa.q: What is a deploy health check for?
qa.right: To confirm the app actually answers after it is released
wrong: To count the lines of code changed
To lock the database during a release
qa.why: A failing probe should fail the deploy.

qa.q: A developer runs git revert on a commit that is already on main. What happens?
qa.right: A new commit is added that undoes the earlier one
wrong: The earlier commit is erased from history
qa.why: Revert is history-preserving.

qa.q: In the gglearn deploy script, why is rsync run with --delete while excluding the SQLite files and .env?
qa.right: Anything not in the source and not excluded would be removed from the server, so the data and secrets must be excluded
wrong: --delete copies the database to the server, so it needs excluding
rsync cannot copy files starting with a dot unless excluded
qa.why: Exclusions protect server-only state from --delete.

qa.q: What does the flock step in the gglearn server commands prevent?
qa.right: Two deploys running on the server at the same time
wrong: The database being read during a build
qa.why: flock serialises deploys on the server.

qa.q: Which Cloudflare SSL mode does ggmoney's DEPLOY.md require?
qa.right: Full (strict)
wrong: Any mode, since the origin is on localhost
qa.why: Flexible would leave the origin hop unencrypted.

qa.q: Which statement about OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect is correct?
qa.right: OpenID Connect adds an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0
wrong: OAuth 2.0 is built on top of OpenID Connect
They are two names for the same protocol
OpenID Connect uses XML assertions like SAML
qa.why: OIDC returns an ID token saying who logged in.

qa.q: Which Git concept is a movable pointer to a commit?
qa.right: A branch
qa.why: Tags are fixed names; branches move as you commit.

qa.q: A team ships a change that passes tests but the site is down after release. Which deploy check catches this?
qa.right: A health probe that expects HTTP 200 from the running app
qa.why: Only a check against the running app proves it came back.

qa.q: Which monitoring signal is a numeric measurement sampled over time?
qa.right: A metric
qa.why: Metrics suit charts and thresholds.

qa.q: A team's pull request builds are failing only on Fridays, passing on rerun with no code change. What is the best description?
qa.right: A flaky test or environment dependency that should be found and fixed
wrong: A reliable test that should be ignored
A sign the linter is misconfigured
qa.why: Intermittent results with no change are flakiness.

qa.q: A developer rebased a branch other people had already pulled and pushed with force. What is the likely consequence?
qa.right: Others have diverging history and may lose or duplicate commits
wrong: Nothing, since rebase never changes hashes
The remote refuses all later pushes permanently
Their local branches update automatically without conflict
qa.why: Rebase rewrites hashes, so shared branches should not be rebased.

qa.q: gglearn's deploy runs drizzle-kit push without --force. What is the effect on a change that would drop a column with data?
qa.right: The deploy stops instead of deleting rows
wrong: The column is dropped after a backup
The deploy ignores the change and continues
qa.why: No --force means destructive changes need a person.

qa.q: After a gglearn deploy, which step decides whether the deploy is reported as successful?
qa.right: Polling http://127.0.0.1:3400/ for HTTP 200
qa.why: The final poll proves the app returned.

qa.q: What is the difference between severity and priority on an issue?
qa.right: Severity measures the damage; priority says how soon to act
wrong: Severity says when; priority measures the damage
They are two names for one field
Severity is set by customers; priority by developers only
qa.why: A cosmetic issue on the home page can be low severity yet high priority.

qa.q: Which is the best reason to use a lockfile in CI?
qa.right: Every run installs the same dependency versions that were tested
wrong: It removes the need for tests
qa.why: Lockfiles make installs repeatable.

qa.q: A production credential is needed by one deploy job only. How should it be handled?
qa.right: Scope it to that job or environment so other jobs cannot read it
wrong: Make it available to every job for simplicity
Commit it to the repository in an encrypted file with the key beside it
Print it in logs so deploys can be debugged
qa.why: Scoping limits the blast radius.

qa.q: Which fits a canary release?
qa.right: Sending the new version to a small share of traffic and watching metrics before widening
wrong: Switching all traffic to a second identical environment at once
Deploying only to the staging environment
qa.why: A canary limits the number of users affected by a bad release.

qa.q: Moksy's CI declares shared secrets once at the top. Why?
qa.right: A copy-per-job approach drifted and one job failed with a too-short secret
wrong: GitHub does not allow secrets inside jobs
Secrets declared once are encrypted more strongly
To make the secrets available to production
qa.why: Declaring once avoids drift.

qa.q: Which describes SSO most accurately?
qa.right: One login gives access to many applications through a central identity provider
wrong: Every application stores its own password
Passwords are shared among team members
Users log in with a hardware key only
qa.why: SSO centralises authentication.

qa.q: Which Apache directive choice makes the gglearn vhost fail closed if the allow-list file is missing?
qa.right: Include (not IncludeOptional)
qa.why: A missing file then stops Apache starting, rather than serving everyone.

qa.q: A team renamed a database column in one release by adding the new column and dropping the old. Rollback now fails. What practice would have avoided this?
qa.right: Expand and contract: add the new column, migrate code, then remove the old in a later release
qa.why: Keeping both versions compatible makes each step reversible.

qa.q: A server accepts traffic directly from the internet as well as via Cloudflare, and rate limiting is easy to evade. What is the root cause?
qa.right: Clients can reach the origin and send a forged X-Forwarded-For
qa.why: Origin lockdown makes the header trustworthy.

qa.q: A developer runs git reset --hard and loses commits. What should they try first?
qa.right: Look in git reflog for the commit and recover it
wrong: Run git gc to repair history
Delete the branch and recreate it
qa.why: Reflog remembers where HEAD pointed.

qa.q: A cloud account is used by a pipeline and its key leaks into a public log. What is the right immediate response?
qa.right: Revoke and rotate the credential, then review what it could access
wrong: Wait to see whether it is used
qa.why: A leaked secret must be treated as compromised.

qa.q: An on-call engineer receives dozens of alerts every night that need no action. What problem is this?
qa.right: Alert fatigue, to be fixed by removing or tuning alerts nobody acts on
wrong: A need for more alert channels
qa.why: Noise hides real alerts.

qa.q: A company wants to ship to production on every green build without a human step. Which practice is that?
qa.right: Continuous deployment
qa.why: Delivery keeps the final release a human decision.

qa.q: Which service type would suit a small event-driven function that is idle most of the time?
qa.right: A serverless function
qa.why: Serverless bills for execution and can scale to zero.

qa.q: You choose a hosted monitoring tool. Which criteria does the track recommend checking?
qa.right: Export, API access, permissions and alert noise
wrong: Number of dashboards shipped by default
Whether the vendor uses the same cloud
qa.why: These keep you from lock-in and noisy alerts.

qa.q: ggsocial's deploy builds into a fresh directory and swaps it in. What is the benefit?
qa.right: The old build keeps serving while the new one compiles
qa.why: A failed build leaves the old one running.

qa.q: Which control gives a pipeline step supply-chain protection against a changed third-party action?
qa.right: Pin it to a specific immutable commit
wrong: Run it without secrets only on Fridays
qa.why: Pinning prevents silent upstream changes.

qa.q: An engineer commits a password, notices, and deletes the file in the next commit. What is the state of the password?
qa.right: Still in history; treat it as compromised and rotate it
qa.why: History keeps the old commit.

qa.q: A team has an error budget nearly spent. What is the sensible action?
qa.right: Slow risky releases and focus on reliability until the budget recovers
qa.why: Spent budget means reliability should take priority.

qa.q: Why can edits to sites-available leave a live HTTPS site unchanged in ggsocial's setup?
qa.right: The live vhost is a copy, not a symlink, so the copy must be edited too
wrong: Apache caches config for a year
The edits need a database push
qa.why: Configtest passes because the live file is untouched.

qa.q: A new teammate pushes a fix straight to main and it breaks the build. What control would have prevented it?
qa.right: Branch protection requiring a pull request and passing checks
qa.why: Protection blocks direct pushes.

qa.q: A deploy script fails halfway because someone started a second deploy at the same moment. What should the script have used?
qa.right: A lock so deploys cannot overlap
qa.why: flock serialises deploys.

qa.q: A team's staging environment passes but production breaks because staging uses a different database engine. What lesson applies?
qa.right: Staging is only useful if it mirrors production closely
wrong: Production should be treated as staging
qa.why: Differences create untested paths.

qa.q: A developer needs one bugfix from a feature branch on the release branch, without the other work. What should they use?
qa.right: git cherry-pick of that commit
wrong: git merge of the whole feature branch
qa.why: Cherry-pick applies a single commit.

qa.q: A team's pipeline is green but customers report errors. Tests all use mocks. What gap is likely?
qa.right: Missing integration and end-to-end coverage against real dependencies
wrong: The build cache is too small
qa.why: Mocks hide real interactions.

qa.q: A leaver still has access to three tools weeks after leaving. What process would have closed this?
qa.right: Provisioning through SCIM and periodic access reviews
qa.why: Central provisioning removes access in every tool.

qa.q: A deploy removed the server's .env file and everyone was logged out. What was probably missing?
qa.right: An rsync exclusion for .env when using --delete
qa.why: With --delete, anything not excluded and absent from source is removed.

qa.q: A project has a backup job but has never restored from one. What risk remains?
qa.right: The backup may be unusable and nobody would know until a disaster
qa.why: Only a restore test proves a backup works.

qa.q: A CI log shows a value from a test secret. The team used dummy CI-only values. What is the impact?
qa.right: Minimal, since the value is not a real credential
qa.why: Dummy values are the point of the habit.

qa.q: A team can only fix a bad release by shipping a new version because the schema has already changed irreversibly. What is this called?
qa.right: Rolling forward
qa.why: A forward fix is the only option.

qa.q: After adding TLS with certbot, the gglearn site is reachable directly from the internet again. What is the most likely cause?
qa.right: The port 443 vhost copy lacks the Include line for the Cloudflare-only block
qa.why: Certbot copies the 80 vhost, and the copy must carry the Include.

qa.q: A trace shows the request spent most of its time in one downstream service. What would you check next?
qa.right: That service's own metrics and logs for the slow period
qa.why: Traces locate the hop; its metrics and logs explain it.

qa.q: A team is tempted to run drizzle-kit push with --force to get past a failing deploy. What should they ask first?
qa.right: Which rows the change would delete, and whether a backup exists
wrong: Whether the deploy is faster with --force
qa.why: Force skips the safeguard against data loss.

qa.q: A script fetches Cloudflare IP lists and writes the allow-list. The fetch returns an empty list. What should the script do?
qa.right: Refuse to write, so an empty allow-list cannot lock everyone out
qa.why: update-cloudflare-ips.sh checks the lists before writing.
